tips.li: A colonist who can't reach a toilet in time goes outside (-3 mood) or soils themselves (-8).
A rough rule: one toilet for every six colonists, close to the bedrooms and the main workrooms.
[lowtech] A latrine needs no research. It fills up and has to be emptied by hand, unless it is plumbed in.
Keep latrines, sewage outlets and burn pits away from wells. Sewage near a well spoils the water.
One toilet to a room, or stall doors between them: someone walked in on feels embarrassed (-3 mood).
A grimy colonist is unhappy (down to -6 mood when filthy). Bad hygiene also raises the chance of food poisoning and makes conversations go worse.
[lowtech] A water tub needs no research. Someone has to keep it filled, though rain fills it too.
A shower is quicker and uses about a third of the water a bathtub does. A bathtub is slower, but very comfortable.
A campfire next to a bathtub heats the water, and a hot bath is a small mood boost (+3).
Dubs Bad Hygiene warns when a well is contaminated and lists what is spoiling it. Move the well or the sources, or build water treatment.
A contaminated water tower stays dirty until it is drained, or until a water treatment system cleans it.
Cholera can kill through dehydration if it isn't treated. Keep the sick in bed with a doctor tending them.
[!lowtech] Two days of toxic fallout spoil the water from ordinary wells. A deep well still draws clean water.
